Hilla, occupied by Abbasid forces in 1163: "Mazyadid rule came to an end"

capitals.name: Kufa
capitals.note: The page says the emirate was centred on the area around Kufa and Hit; it names no capital before Hilla, so Kufa is the researcher's reading.

capitals.name: Hilla
capitals.note: Infobox capital Hilla (no year). The page says Ali founded Hilla in 1012 and that it became the capital with its wall under Sadaqa I (1086-1108); the traditional founding by Sadaqa in 1102 is not on the page.

rulers.name: Ali I ibn Mazyad
rulers.note: c. 961-1017; the page says his reign "must be dated a half century earlier" than older sources

rulers.name: Sadaqa I ibn Mansur
rulers.note: defeated and killed in battle in 1108; "king of the Arabs" to the First Crusaders

rulers.name: Muhalhil ibn Ali
rulers.note: end date unknown; infobox says the dynasty ends c. 1160, the text says Hilla was occupied in 1163

correction.text: the area around Kufa and Hit in central Iraq

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mazyadid row): "the emirate ruled the area around Kufa and Hit in central Iraq", the lands granted by Mu'izz al-Dawla. The page gives no area; the shape (Kufa, Babil, Karbala and a circle at Hit) is a reading of "between Kufa and Hit". The Uqaylid page puts "Kufa and Hilla (Jami'yan)" in a 996 treaty for al-Muqallad, so the same land carries a rival claim; the Mazyadid page mentions no Uqaylid loss.

ledger.note: c. 961: the Buyids settle the Banu Asad between Kufa and Hit. 'Between 956 and 963, the Buyid emir Mu'izz al-Dawla granted the Mazyadids titles, subsidies, and lands between Kufa and Hit in return for military service' (infobox 'c.961').

1086: Hilla becomes the Mazyadid capital. The page: Hilla, founded in 1012 by Ali, 'became the capital' and Sadaqa I (1086-1108) had a wall built around it; the move year is Sadaqa's accession, bridging.

region.text: Hilla and the Mazyadid lands around Kufa and Hit

ledger.note: 1163: Abbasid forces occupy Hilla. 'In 1163, Hilla was occupied by Abbasid forces' and 'Mazyadid rule came to an end' (infobox c. 1160).
1163: the Mazyadid emirate ends with the Abbasid occupation of Hilla.

wars.name: Seljuk war against Sadaqa I
wars.outcome: Sadaqa I, at the height of his power under the weak Barkiyaruq (1092-1105), was "defeated and killed in battle in 1108" by the Seljuk sultan's army; Dubays II succeeded and Hilla stayed Mazyadid.
wars.note: The page names the sultan as Malik-Shah II "after Barkiyaruq" and gives no year for the start of the war, so only 1108 is recorded; no border moved.

wars.name: Mazyadid-Zengi war against the Abbasid caliph and Seljuks
wars.outcome: Zengi defeated Dubays II at the Battle of Mubarraqiyya (March 1123); on 20 June 1132 Dubays and Zengi were defeated by the caliph al-Mustarshid at Hisn al-Baramika, north of Baghdad. No border moved.

certainty.note: A tribal emirate with a core at Kufa, Hit and Hilla; the pages give no frontiers and no area.

notes: Cliopatria has no Mazyadid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. 'Mazyadid dynasty' is a disambiguation page (with the Yazidids of Shirvan, 861-1027, a different dynasty: see shirvan, eu-19); the article is Banu Mazyad. All four pages are thin on territory: no area, no gains or losses with years, no mention of Wasit, Anbar, Takrit, Basra or Mosul as Mazyadid. Not written as events (page silent or undated): the Uqaylid claim to Kufa and Hilla (Jami'yan) by the 996 treaty with Baha' al-Dawla (Uqaylid page); Dubays I's support for al-Basasiri and the Fatimids in 1058-59 (no territorial result on the page); Seljuk forces occupying Hilla 'several times' (undated); Dubays II's flights and the Aleppo siege of 1124-25; the Mazyadid support for Qirwash against the Oghuz at Mosul in 1044 (Uqaylid page). Dates that differ: Hilla founded 1012 by Ali (this page) vs 1102 by Sadaqa (tradition, not opened); end c. 1160 (infobox) vs 1163 (text) vs Muhalhil's reign 1150-?; Ali I's reign 'must be dated a half century earlier' than older sources. The Buyid suzerainty and later Seljuk and Abbasid overlordship are vassal relations the suzerains' dossiers should carry; none is dated on these pages. Gazetteer names needed: Hit (drawn as a coordinate), Hilla resolves via Al Hillah.
